questions.problem: Find, in descending powers of $z,$ the first three terms of the binomial expansion of ${(1-{z}^{2})}^{4}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's compare our expression with the binomial

$$
(a+b)^{n}.
$$

Here we have that $n=4,$ $a=1,$ and $b=-{z}^{2}.$ So, the exponents of the binomial expansion must follow the pattern

$$
{a}^{4}{b}^{0},\,{a}^{3}{b}^{1},\,{a}^{2}{b}^{2},\,{a}^{1}{b}^{3},\,{a}^{0}{b}^{4}.
$$

The $4$th row in Pascal's Triangle is $(1,4,6,4,1).$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1-{z}^{2})}^{4} & =1{a}^{4}+4{a}^{3}b+6{a}^{2}{b}^{2}+4a{b}^{3}+1{b}^{4} \\  & =1(1)^{4}(-{z}^{2})^{0}+4(1)^{3}(-{z}^{2})^{1}+6(1)^{2}(-{z}^{2})^{2}+4(1)^{1}(-{z}^{2})^{3}+1(1)^{0}(-{z}^{2})^{4} \\  & =1(1)(1)+4(1)(-{z}^{2})+6(1)({z}^{4})+4(1)(-{z}^{6})+1(1)({z}^{8}) \\  & =1-4{z}^{2}+6{z}^{4}-4{z}^{6}+{z}^{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

We rewrite the binomial expansion in descending powers of $z$ as follows:

$$
(1-{z}^{2})^{4}={z}^{8}-4{z}^{6}+6{z}^{4}-4{z}^{2}+1
$$

Finally, in descending powers of $z,$ the first three terms of the binomial expansion are

$$
{z}^{8}-4{z}^{6}+6{z}^{4}.
$$
